scientific_source.citation: Gauss J., Scheipl F., Herrmann M., 'DCSI -- An improved measure of cluster separability based on separation and connectedness'
scientific_source.extraction_method: MathML alttext (LaTeX) parsed directly from the arXiv HTML rendering; definitions were NOT reconstructed from prose or recollection

definition.input: X (n x d numeric) and a partition into classes C_1..C_K; a distance metric d (Euclidean by default)

MinPts.paper_quote: In this paper - unless otherwise stated - MinPts = 5 is always used, similar to DBSCAN
MinPts.interpretation: minimal cluster size: an isolated set of at least this many close points is not discarded as noise

epsilon_i.plain: for each class i, the MEDIAN over its points of the distance to that point's (2*MinPts)-th nearest neighbour WITHIN the same class
epsilon_i.why_per_class: densities differ between classes, so a single global epsilon can leave low-density classes with no core points at all

key_differences_from_dbscan: core points are computed SEPARATELY for each class
the epsilon-neighbourhood contains ONLY observations from the same class
the point itself is excluded from its own neighbourhood
the comparison is >= MinPts on the neighbourhood EXCLUDING self

separation.plain: minimum distance between the CORE points of the two classes
separation.rationale: robust to outliers by construction and unchanged by observations irrelevant to separability

connectedness.plain: the LARGEST edge weight in a minimum spanning tree built only on the CORE points of a class; then the maximum over the two classes
connectedness.rationale: distinguishes connectedness from compactness, so non-compact shapes such as rings are not penalised

limits: DCSI -> 0 when Sep -> 0 or Conn -> infinity

multi_class_aggregation.plain: unweighted MEAN of all K(K-1)/2 pairwise DCSI values
multi_class_aggregation.authors_recommendation: the mean pairwise DCSI is the authors' recommended multi-class summary (Appendix C.2)

frozen_parameters.epsilon_rule: per-class median distance to the (2*MinPts)-th within-class nearest neighbour

edge_case_policy.one_cluster_partition: INVALID(fewer_than_two_clusters) -- no pair exists, so the aggregation is undefined
edge_case_policy.class_with_zero_core_points: INVALID(dcsi_no_core_points) for the affected PAIR -- Sep and Conn are both undefined without core points
edge_case_policy.class_with_one_core_point: MST over a single vertex has no edges, so Conn(C_i) is defined as 0 for that class; if the resulting Conn (max over the pair) is 0 see zero_connectedness
edge_case_policy.zero_connectedness: if Conn == 0 while Sep > 0 then q -> infinity and DCSI -> 1; reported as VALID 1.0 (the supremum), which is the mathematical limit
edge_case_policy.zero_separation: if Sep == 0 then q = 0 and DCSI = 0; VALID
edge_case_policy.duplicate_observations: permitted; unlike CVDD, DCSI's MST enters only through its MAXIMUM edge weight, which is identical for every minimum spanning tree even when the MST itself is non-unique, so duplicates do not create ambiguity
edge_case_policy.noise_labels: the paper defines DCSI over a partition into classes; a negative/noise label is treated as its own class only if the caller supplies it as such. Our wrapper EXCLUDES label -1 from the class set and records it, because a noise label is not a class in the paper's sense
edge_case_policy.insufficient_points_for_epsilon: if a class has fewer than 2*MinPts+1 members, the (2*MinPts)-th within-class neighbour does not exist; the largest available neighbour distance is used, which is the natural continuous extension and is documented rather than silently imputed
